subject: [PATCH v2 0/6] memcg: Batch mod_memcg_state() for MEMCG_SOCK.

reviews.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kuniyuki Iwashima noted that migrating to objcg would add an indirect layer and costs for css_tryget() / css_put(), and suggested inlining __consume_stock() or batching in memcg_stock as crucial steps.

reviewer suggested batching mod_memcg_state() for MEMCG_KMEM, but noted that some stats already have specialized batching
reviews.raw_body:
sk_forward_alloc is already batched per page, and I think
migrating to objcg would just add an indirect layer and some
costs for css_tryget() / css_put(), and still inlining
__consume_stock() or batching in memcg_stock would be crucial.

---

I guess you mean optimising MEMCG_SOCK along with MEMCG_KMEM (or
mod_memcg_state() / memcg_rstat_updated() in general).

I can give it a try, though some stats already have specialised
batching (e.g. NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B in obj_stock and folio stats
in uncharge_batch()).

reviews.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that patch 5 provides a significant throughput gain on the platform mentioned in patch 4, but __css_rstat_updated() spends more cycles.
sentiment_signals: requested additional analysis of performance metrics
reviews.raw_body:
Interestingly, patch 5 only (without patch 4) gives even more
throughput gain on the platform mentioned in patch 4.

But as expected, __css_rstat_updated() spends more cycles.

  tcp_rr (10000 flows, 128 threads, 60s, average of 3 runs):

  Metric                     |       Baseline |   Patched  |    Diff
  ---------------------------+----------------+---------------------+--------
  Throughput (RPS)           |     20,884,499 | 28,453,051 | +36.24%
  Latency Mean (us)          |         478.46 |     351.07 | -26.63%
  Latency p50 (us)           |         453.96 |     343.04 | -24.43%
  Latency p90 (us)           |         669.00 |     479.57 | -28.32%
  Latency p99 (us)           |         969.38 |     593.92 | -38.73%

  perf cycles (10000 flows, 10s, average of 3 runs):

  Server (M cycles / %)      |           Baseline |            Patched |    Diff
  ---------------------------+--------------------+-----------------------+--------
  Host Total Cycles          |        4,566,914 M |        4,548,747 M |   -0.4%
  tcp_rcv_established()      | 158,009 M (3.460%) | 158,773 M (3.490%) |   +0.5%
  mem_cgroup_sk_charge()     |  18,420 M (0.403%) |  16,211 M (0.356%) |  -12.0%
  mem_cgroup_sk_uncharge()   |  16,593 M (0.363%) |  12,121 M (0.266%) |  -27.0%
  __css_rstat_updated()      |   3,502 M (0.077%) |   5,606 M (0.123%) |  +60.0%
  Memcg Sock Total           |  38,515 M (0.843%) |  33,937 M (0.746%) |  -11.9%

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about the future impact of moving kernel objects to objcg infrastructure on zombie memcgs, explaining that network sockets are not currently urgent but will eventually be affected and may require indirection for measurement.
reviews.raw_body:
We are over time moving kernel objects holding direct reference to memcg to the
objcg infra and the reason is such objects can become source of zombie memcgs.
There is no urgency for the network sockets but eventually it will happen. We
will see if indirection is really measurable at that time.

reviews.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kuniyuki Iwashima reported a ~5% regression in performance with the patch, but noted that optimizing stats reduced it to ~2%, and suggested accepting the patch due to its overall perf gain.
reviews.raw_body:
I tried it yesterday and saw ~5% regression w/ tcp_rr 10k/20k flows,
https://github.com/q2ven/linux/commit/7407580c37784bf594fede4d6da6b266d8c7a11d

but optimising stats limited it to ~2%.
https://github.com/q2ven/linux/commit/1ffc01395156b278c3d1c9c5fff7b9484f632be8

Given the perf gain by this series, I guess it's acceptable
and I can post it to net-next once merge window opens.
(rstats patch will be a follow-up after v3)

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where the mod_memcg_state() function is called multiple times for each socket, leading to inefficiencies. The patches batch these calls together, reducing overhead and improving performance. The changes are targeted at MEMCG_SOCK, correcting a typo in the original code.
